extracted.intended_audience: patent searchers / IP analysts / Orbit Intelligence users (training seminar attendees)
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Orbit Intelligence platform to perform FTO (freedom-to-operate) and patentability searches, manage results, run analytics, and maintain workfiles/lists for IP analysis. Covers database selection, field/date/geographic limits, result inspection, research tools, saving/exporting, workfile workflows, and platform analytics/metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: FamPat vs FullPat (family vs individual records)
rubrics_metrics.description: FamPat: Patents protecting the same invention in different countries are grouped in a family. FullPat: Patents protecting the same invention in different countries are individual records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose FamPat when you want de-duplicated, family-level views (e.g., patentability review across jurisdictions). Choose FullPat when you need to analyze individual country-level records (e.g., FTO by country).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred database for FTO searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred database: FullPat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on individual countries and use native language when possible. FullPat gives individual records useful to determine if an alive patent in a specific country can block freedom to operate.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTO legal-status limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal status: Only alive patents can block you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: choose the filter 'Alive' when running an FTO, but be careful with lapsed publications (they may appear alive/dead inconsistently).

rubrics_metrics.name: FTO validity-date limitation (remaining patent life)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity date of the patents: if the patent is lapsed/dead/expired, you are typically free to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: choose 'Priority date' and search '21 years ago to present' to capture patents still within typical term limits for blocking activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTO geographic limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific geographic areas: where you are trying to determine FTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: consider searching by country level for clearance in a particular country (FullPat helps with country-level records).

rubrics_metrics.name: FTO field limitation (claims focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field: claims characterize and limit the scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: choose the 'Claims' field when doing FTO searches because claims define the enforceable scope that can block practice in a jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability search preferred database
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred database: FamPat (faster review: no duplicates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FamPat groups family members so you can review inventions without duplicate family members; use FamPat when assessing novelty/inventive step across publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability: no date/geographic/field limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitation: No date limit: any prior art can block you. No geographic limit: any prior art can block you. No Field limitation: any prior art disclosed in the description is sufficient to destroy novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: for patentability searches choose 'Alive or Dead' and search 'All publications'; use 'Full Text' (search description/objects, not only claims) because disclosure anywhere in the document can anticipate novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search by invention vs search by publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Search by publication: FullPat database. Search by invention: FamPat database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FullPat for publication-level, country-specific FTO work; use FamPat for invention-level, family de-duplicated patentability or landscape searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections availability and user settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Available collections are FamPat, FullPat and Fulltext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check user settings to ensure you can search all available collections: account menu -> enable option YES -> confirm. After that, 3 collections are available in the advanced search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field limitation summary for FTO vs patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: No field limitation: Full Text (patentability). Field limitation: Claims (FTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Claims field when limiting to enforceable scope (FTO). Use Full Text when doing novelty searches where any disclosure suffices to destroy novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results display customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Customize hitlist display, display the Preview tab, select the tabs to display, automatic sorting of results by relevance, representative member shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preview and representative member to focus on claims of a member; customize which tabs show (KWIC, Highlighting) and configure automatic sorting to speed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: KWIC and highlight for term distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: KWIC (Key Word In Context): to display the distribution in the family of terms searched on the basis of the search fields. Highlighting: ability to add highlighted words and save the highlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use KWIC to see where searched terms appear across family members and to guide selection of representative members or to spot relevant disclosures quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter and view document features
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter: allows to filter the result of a search (three options by default, possibility to add). View document: allows clicking on the title to view a particular family and focus on claims of a member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filters to narrow results and 'View document' to inspect family member claims; filters and views improve triage efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection controls for result lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection button: Click all records button to select the entire families. Check box at the top of the results list selects the current page. Number of selected families indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use selection controls to bulk-select families for export, similarity, or saving to lists/workfiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity research tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of one or several families (up to 10,000). 1st option: find similar patents in all database. 2nd option: find similar patents only in the results of the selection list. List organized by relevance; relevance score displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarity is calculated on similarity, classifications and citations. Use KWIC to determine similar values per family. Use similarity to define new keywords, identify similar concepts, or refine queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations research tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations allows finding the cited families (prior art) on the basis of relevance (examiners and applicants). Display categories: citing, cited. Citations Tab: examiners and applicants, literature cited for a family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use citations to build prior art trees, identify examiner-cited references, and view citation networks; graphical display is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export and save options
rubrics_metrics.description: Export Menu: XLSX. New Export Menu: XLSX. Save search: ability to save search script or execute manually; no limit on saved searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use export to extract hitlists or data for reporting. Save search scripts for rerunning or alerting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists vs Workfiles vs Directories (saving semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists: related to the search module; allows to save the results of one or more searches. No limit on number of lists. Automatic update of families when the list is opened. Ability to cross contents of a list with another question. Lists are not workfiles. Directories are the only items that can be shared and evaluated. Workfiles are linked to the folders module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lists for dynamic saved search results; use directories/workfiles for archived, shareable, evaluable portfolios. Know that workfiles are static except manual updates or alert feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workfile uses and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The Workfile is defined by four uses: Archive (archiving patent families and designs), Review (stars, notes, attachments, personal fields), Share (creation of Group readers), Operate (integrated module search, analysis module available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize work into directories and folders; share at the directory level; Inbox is a default directory that cannot be shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workfile archive/feed constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Feed of the patent families from the search module (search, list or alert) or from Workfile module (import number). Limit number families in contractual records. A family or design can be in multiple folders. The tag NEW on a family is present for a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating feeds from alerts: Only one directory can be selected; the workfile will be created during the first run of the alert; an alert cannot be sent into an existing folder; updates depend on monitoring code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review features: stars, notes, attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Stars: From 0 to 5 stars assigned to a family; stars are exportable and filterable. Notes: notes assigned to a family, compilation of attributed notes, possibility to modify/delete; notes are exportable, filterable and searchable. Attachments: allocation to a family (8 max) or a Workfile (8 max); attachments are searchable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stars/notes/attachments for internal triage and to make portfolios reviewable and shareable; be mindful of attachment limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal (user) fields in Workfiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal fields: creation requires defining the list of values. 100 user fields max. One single type of field internal classification. Internal classification/multi-values selector: multiple values per field. Single value selector: one value per field. User fields are exportable, filterable and searchable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and allocate personal fields to families or selections of families to implement internal taxonomies and facilitate filtering/reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share: readers and experts access model
rubrics_metrics.description: Email address and password are the identifiers for readers to access the Workfiles interface and to share documents. Associate a reader or an expert with a directory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share at the directory level; manage access via reader/expert credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate: filters, research, and updates within workfiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate: Filter a folder or directory (filter deleted when viewing another folder). Research: selecting a folder, directory or entire portfolio and different data types usable for search; unwanted items and trash are searchable only. Update: update of selected families; update the contents of families (new members, new information etc.); tag 'updated' is present on the family for a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use operate functions to maintain portfolios, run targeted searches across saved sets, and track updates with tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settings and user preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Account preferences include: number of results per page, mail notification, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Configure display and notification preferences to align the interface with your review/alerting workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytics feature levels and limits (Essential/Advanced/Premium)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of features linked to the analysis level (Essential, Advanced, Premium) with limits: Max families in live analysis, Max families in saved analysis, Metrics in analysis, Benchmark graphs, Evaluation modules, Landscape map, Custom axis, Export all data, Filter, Drill down, Multiple selection, Color by, Graph templates, Concepts analysis, Cloud chart, Data rules, One click report, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a subscription level that matches your analysis scale (family counts, metrics needed, and visualization/export capabilities). Check exact numeric limits (e.g., 100k/300k/2M families) and which features (concept analysis, landscape maps) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Impact metric
rubrics_metrics.description: The Technical Impact is based on forward citations which are adapted depending on the nature of the citation (self/non-self), the age, and technical domain of the patent. LOG progression has also been used to model the increase of a patent’s impact. Results are normalized so that the average patent has a score of 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret technical impact as a normalized citation-weighted score where early citations contribute more (log progression) and adjustments are made for self-citations, age, and domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market Strategy Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of the market in the countries where patents are pending or have been granted (size calculated using GDP). A reduction of 40% is given to pending countries. WO/EP figures are calculated based on the countries where WO/EPs tend to be granted. Countries where patents were granted but are now dead are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market Strategy measures geographic market reach and adjusts for pending filings and country grant likelihood; used as a component in patent strength computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Strength Index
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Strength is based on Technical Impact and Market Strategy. They are weighted and summed. The weight values have been calculated in order to give high scores to patents which have been litigated. Patent strength is available for both alive and dead patents. Results are normalized so that the average patent has a score of 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use patent strength to gauge combined technical and market importance; note weighting favors litigated patents and that the index is normalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Value Index and Portfolio Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Value index = Patent Strength index x Remaining Life. The patent value is based on the Patent Strength index with a weighting based on the remaining life of the patent. Patent value is available only for alive patents. The Portfolio Value is based on the sum of Patent Value Indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret patent value as strength adjusted for remaining term (only for alive patents); sum patent values to obtain portfolio-level valuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity/citation-based calculations and selection scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarity lists are organized by relevance (relevance score display) and similarity is calculated on: similarity, classifications and citations. Selection of one or several families up to 10,000 for similarity operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When running similarity analyses, expect relevance rankings based on combined similarity/classification/citation signals and be mindful of the selection upper bound (10k families).
